verdicts.title: Missing viewport-fit=cover defeats every env(safe-area-inset-*) rule on iOS
verdicts.reason: Confirmed at frontend/index.html:14 — viewport meta lacks viewport-fit=cover. This is a well-established WebKit behavior: env(safe-area-inset-*) resolves to 0 unless the page opts into the full display area with viewport-fit=cover, so all CSS relying on those insets (safe-area padding for topbar, actions menu, note pane, standalone PWA header) would collapse on notched/Dynamic Island iPhones, worst in the installed PWA due to apple-mobile-web-app-capable=yes at line 7. Real defect.

verdicts.title: theme-color meta is a static light color and is never updated for dark mode
verdicts.reason: Confirmed only one static theme-color meta exists (index.html:8, #f4f1e8) with no media query variant, and grep across frontend/src finds zero other references to theme-color, meaning nothing updates it at runtime when the theme is cycled or system dark mode is active under theme=auto. This produces a light chrome/status-bar color clash in dark mode on iOS Safari/PWA and Android Chrome, a genuine defect.

verdicts.title: Missing viewport-fit=cover defeats every env(safe-area-inset-*) rule on iOS
verdicts.reason: Verified: index.html:14 viewport meta is `width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0` with no viewport-fit=cover, and env(safe-area-inset-*) is genuinely used in topbar.css:4/7-8, responsive.css:10/53/86-87/95/144/148, note-content.css:165, and noteEnhancements.css:185/187/241/286 as claimed. Per WebKit spec, safe-area-inset-* env() variables resolve to 0 unless the page opts into viewport-fit=cover, so all these calc() expressions collapse to their base values on notched/Dynamic Island iPhones, producing exactly the described UI bugs (actions menu under home indicator, PWA header underlapping status bar/notch). apple-mobile-web-app-capable=yes at line 7 is also confirmed, making the installed PWA path fullscreen and thus most affected. This is a real, verifiable defect.

verdicts.title: Missing viewport-fit=cover defeats every env(safe-area-inset-*) rule on iOS
verdicts.reason: Confirmed at frontend/index.html:14 — the viewport meta tag is `width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0` with no `viewport-fit=cover`. This is a well-documented WebKit requirement: env(safe-area-inset-*) only resolves to non-zero values when the page opts into the full display area via viewport-fit=cover; otherwise all insets are 0. apple-mobile-web-app-capable=yes is also present at line 7, confirming this app supports installed PWA/standalone mode on iOS, which is exactly where notched/Dynamic-Island devices make this matter most. The finding correctly identifies a real, verifiable defect on a named target client (iOS Safari / installed iOS PWA) with no dependency on unverified downstream CSS specifics.
